results.title: Who wants unions?
results.creator_credit: ONF | NFB, Mark Zannis, Laszlo Barna and Laura Alper
results.brief_description: Juxtaposing the views of those who don’t want unions and those who do, this film examines new management techniques that have led to a steady decrease in unionization and an increase in union-free work environments. The film features portions of a lecture given by Charles Hughes, American management consultant and North American guru of the union-free model, whose Long-Range Maintenance Model has been widely adopted. As can be seen in the film, present-day management techniques are much more subtle and sophisticated than the goon squad union-busting activities that once made headlines.

results.title: Who wants to be a princess anyway?
results.creator_credit: Film Australia, Tristram Miall and Susan Cornwell
results.brief_description: Why do boys receive more attention in the classroom than girls do? This video examines a gender equity program operating in primary schools to encourage girls to develop an awareness of the range of career and educational options available to them, in particular, in the fields of maths and science. Some classes in a co-educational primary school are conducted as single-sex classes to develop the confidence of the girls.

results.title: Who robbed the robins?
results.brief_description: A delightful animated story: A family of robins have their eggs stolen by another bird. Father robin hires a detective to recover their eggs. The eggs are returned safely to mother and father robin and the villain is taken into custody. The three eggs hatch and the robin family live happily ever after. Animation by H.J Whitaker. Music composed and orchestrated by Jose Norman. Designed by Alan Carter.

results.title: Who needs rules?
results.creator_credit: Encyclopaedia Britannica Films and Gregory Heimer
results.brief_description: This film shows the wide range of rules of society, from everyday rules to the complex rules of law. Gives two examples: two children decide whether or not to keep a stray dog in an apartment prohibiting animals; and a boy involved in a playground row is torn between the school rule against fighting and his father’s order to defend himself. Suitable for upper primary and lower secondary levels.

results.title: Who needs a wash?
results.creator_credit: Royal Society for the Protection of Birds and Hugh Miles
results.brief_description: A passionate and ecological film for the defence of ‘The Wash’. ‘The Wash’ is an estuary mud flat up to five miles wide that is washed by tides from the North Sea. Many birds and sea creatures call ‘The Wash’ home, or a t least a resting place. Flora abounds on the land edges. Acre for acre there is more protein in tidal mud banks than in reclaimed grain fields. Proposed fresh water reservoirs may pose a threat to wildlife.
